assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. The path from proglucagon processing and incretin physiology to long-acting agonists is clear, original and of exceptional lasting medical impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and gut-hormone physiology), Holst (physiology and characterization of active GLP-1) and Knudsen (design of long-acting liraglutide/semaglutide) form a coherent three-person configuration. Mojsov's contribution (identification of the active peptide) and other early contributors make credit contested; only listed names can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized trials and broad clinical uptake over nearly two decades; timing is strongly favorable and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the early peptide-identification contributors (notably Mojsov) versus physiology and drug-design contributions is unresolved.
Whether the prize should reward the physiology or the pharmaceutical development is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave experimentalists millisecond, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is now a standard tool across neuroscience, with expanding uses beyond the brain. The method is original, conceptually clear and has reshaped experimental physiology.
assessment.attribution: A compound discovery: channelrhodopsin characterization (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann), first neuronal demonstration and tool development (Boyden, Deisseroth), and earlier genetically targeted photostimulation (Miesenboeck). Six credited names exceed three; the chosen trio spans microbial opsin biology and neuronal deployment, but Nagel and Bamberg are arguably equally decisive.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: two decades of independent use, reproducibility and the first clinical translation in vision restoration.
uncertainties: Truncating six credited contributors to three is inherently contentious.
Clinical therapeutic impact is still early; the case rests mainly on tool impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV cancers, with population-level evidence of near-elimination of high-grade lesions and falling cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated cohorts. The VLP concept is original and the public-health impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity at NCI) and Frazer (VLP work with Zhou, who has died) are a plausible trio; this partly overlaps with zur Hausen's prior recognition for HPV-cancer link. Contributions of other groups (e.g., Rose, Kirnbauer) and commercial developers are not represented in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: licensed since 2006, with long-term efficacy and effectiveness data now showing cancer reductions.
uncertainties: Priority among independent VLP groups and posthumous contribution of Jian Zhou complicate credit.
Prior HPV Nobel recognition may reduce the sense of novelty for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed, linking infection, autoimmunity, senescence and cancer immunotherapy. It is a conceptually clean and original mechanism with a clear causal chain from cGAMP second-messenger discovery to receptor and adaptor.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP as second messenger; Barber identified STING as an essential adaptor. Ishikawa co-discovered STING and Sun and Wu were first authors on cGAS work, so a two-person prize would omit contributors from the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature mechanistically with strong independent confirmation, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved drugs.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is not yet established.
Attribution of STING discovery among Barber, Ishikawa and others is partly contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and successors turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of targeting a driver oncogene. Impact on patients and on oncology drug development is profound and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical proof of concept), Lydon (medicinal chemistry/target program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural configuration. The discovery of BCR-ABL itself (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) is outside the credited set, and Lydon's role is an industry contribution; Nobel precedent has been cautious about drug development.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with 20+ years of survival data; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize tradition favors the underlying oncogene biology over the drug development.
Roles of the original Ciba-Geigy chemists such as Zimmermann are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells provide durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics. The concept, engineering and clinical validation are original and the impact on hematologic oncology is substantial.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and CAR design) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early CAR clinical work) is a plausible trio; Eshhar and others are not in the credited list and the first-CAR concept credit is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: approved products since 2017 with durable responses, but long-term safety, solid-tumor limits and manufacturing constraints remain.
uncertainties: Credit for foundational CAR design versus clinical translation is unresolved.
Long-term durability and secondary malignancy risk are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single Lgr5+ adult stem cells self-organize into long-lived epithelial organoids, creating a platform for modeling development, infection, cancer and personalized medicine. The finding is original and has spread across many fields of biology.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid work, with Sato the first author of the key intestinal organoid papers. This two-person configuration is clean from the supplied credit; Yamanaka-type and earlier 3D culture precedents are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Maturity is good for research use, but clinical or therapeutic impact (drug screening, transplantation) is still emerging, so the case rests on tool impact.
uncertainties: Translational and clinical impact remain limited.
Whether Sato's role is distinct enough for laureate status is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response explains how cells sense ER stress and adjust folding capacity, with consequences for diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease. It is a foundational and original piece of cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified the Ire1/Hac1 signaling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with Mori providing the HAC1/UPRE and Walter the Ire1 kinase/RNase and splicing mechanism. A two-person configuration is plausible, though Ron's contribution to the PERK/eIF2 arm is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature with strong independent confirmation over three decades; therapeutic translation is partial and still developing.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is modest so far.
The PERK/ATF6 arms involve contributors not in the credited names.
